problems.stem: A teaching-philosophy statement says: "I believe AI should empower every learner." Which revision turns this into a defensible professional stance rather than a slogan?
options: "I believe AI is the future of education and embrace it fully."
"I will use AI tools for formative feedback but keep grading and disclosure decisions with the teacher, because students must know when their work is read by a model."
"I believe AI should empower and inspire every single learner equally."
"I am cautiously optimistic about AI and will see how it goes."
problems.explanation: A professional philosophy commits to a specific stance with a named boundary and a reason, not an aspirational slogan.

problems.stem: A reviewer annotates a philosophy statement: "Your values section says you prioritize student autonomy, but your practice section has the AI auto-correct student answers before they submit. These contradict." What does this note ask the writer to fix?
options: Delete the practice section so only the stated values remain.
Add a citation to an autonomy theorist next to the values claim.
Align the stated value with an actual classroom practice, or revise the value so the philosophy is internally consistent.
Make the autonomy sentence longer and more confident.
problems.explanation: A professional philosophy must show consistency between stated values and the practices the teacher actually commits to.

problems.stem: A candidate asks BigAL to write their entire teaching-philosophy statement and submits it unchanged. Beyond academic-honesty issues, why does this most undermine the artifact's purpose?
options: The model writes too formally for a philosophy statement.
A teaching philosophy is supposed to disclose the author's own committed values and judgment; outsourcing it leaves no actual professional stance to defend in an interview or classroom.
The statement would be too short to meet the length requirement.
AI text always contains factual errors about education law.
problems.explanation: The artifact's whole purpose is to make the teacher's own values inspectable; a generated stance cannot be defended as the teacher's judgment.

problems.stem: Which philosophy statement would best survive a skeptical hiring committee asking, "What would you NOT do with AI, even if it saved time?"
options: One that lists every AI tool the candidate has tried.
One that says AI should always be used to maximize efficiency.
One that names a specific line the teacher will not cross (for example, never letting AI assign final grades without human review) and gives the value that draws the line.
One that avoids mentioning AI to stay neutral.
problems.explanation: A defensible philosophy names its limits, not only its enthusiasms; a stated boundary with a reason shows committed judgment.

problems.stem: Provide a concise response that demonstrates this learning objective: Document a bounded AI/software support move with accepted and rejected suggestions.
problems.expected_answer: The response accurately demonstrates the section objective: Document a bounded AI/software support move with accepted and rejected suggestions, using relevant section concepts, evidence, or calculations.
problems.explanation: This direct-evidence item is used when no closed-response item adequately samples the objective. Score it with the section concepts and worked examples as the rubric.
